'''Marcel Berger''' (14 April 1927 – 15 October 2016) was a French [[mathematician]], working in the field of [[differential geometry]], and a former director of the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]] (IHÉS), France.

==Biography==
After studying from 1948 to 1951 at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]] in Paris, Berger obtained in 1954 his PhD from the [[University of Paris]], with thesis written under the direction of [[André Lichnerowicz]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=36696}}</ref> From 1958 to 1964 he taught at the [[University of Strasbourg]] and had visiting positions at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] and the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. From 1964 to 1966 he taught at the [[Université Nice-Sophia-Antipolis|University of Nice]], after which he joined the [[Paris Diderot University|University of Paris VII]]. From 1985 to 1993 he served as director of the IHÉS. He was President of the [[Société mathématique de France|French Mathematical Society]] in 1979–1980.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://smf.emath.fr/content/anciens-presidents |title=Anciens Présidents &#124; Société Mathématique de France |access-date=2016-10-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161024023304/http://smf.emath.fr/content/anciens-presidents |archive-date=2016-10-24 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Formerly residing in Le Castera in [[Lasseube]], Berger was instrumental in [[Mikhail Gromov (mathematician)|Mikhail Gromov]]'s accepting positions both at the University of Paris and at the IHÉS.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://smf.emath.fr/content/d%C3%A9c%C3%A8s-de-marcel-berger |title=Décès de Marcel Berger &#124; Société Mathématique de France |access-date=2016-10-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161022191528/http://smf.emath.fr/content/d%C3%A9c%C3%A8s-de-marcel-berger |archive-date=2016-10-22 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
